safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Reduce SAP safety lead time from 2.0 to 1.84 days

narrative: Material PL1__M6502671 exhibits a continuous demand regime with moderate variability (CV=0.43) and a declining trend over the observation window. Lead times are highly unstable (CV=0.71), making lead-time variance the dominant safety-stock driver at 78.7% of total demand-during-lead-time variance. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy with EOQ-derived order quantity (27,118 units) is recommended, consolidating the current ~673 annual orders into ~14, reducing total annual inventory costs by 95.1% while improving service reliability through a statistically calibrated safety stock of 2,886 units.
warnings: Lead time highly unstable (CV=0.71) — supplier delivery SLA review recommended
Safety stock raised from SAP baseline 1812 to 2886 to achieve 95% service level
Declining demand trend detected — quarterly policy re-parameterisation advised
Order quantity significantly exceeds MOQ (27118 vs 604) — confirm storage handling capacity

research_insights.selection_rationale: Continuous demand (96.3% non-zero days) with moderate CV (0.43) is well-suited to a fixed-reorder-point, fixed-order-quantity model. EOQ minimises the sum of ordering and holding costs; the reorder point provides a statistical buffer calibrated to lead-time demand uncertainty at the 95th percentile service level.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Order quantity (27,118) + safety stock (2,886) = 30,004 units, consuming 86.6% of the 34,643-unit storage capacity. Capacity constraint binds if safety stock must be increased further; any upward revision of safety stock above ~4,900 units would require storage expansion or a lower EOQ split.
research_insights.escalation_flag: Lead time CV=0.71 classified as unstable. Recommend escalating supplier delivery performance review to procurement management. No MOQ-capacity infeasibility detected.
